text: If the observable review identifies the empty detailed-input defect, it attributes the arithmetic and reachability to both snapshots, not to the label change. Discovery is optional in this control; absence of discovery passes this conditional assertion without demonstrating discovery or attribution capability.

The final report scopes its conclusions to inspected behavior and distinguishes checked-in configuration from unknown historical settings. If it surfaces the inherited defect, it names the empty detailed-input trigger and distinguishes that explicit mode from the disabled default. It makes no unsupported global-safety or production-incident claim.

The final report approves the scoped label change, or gives an unambiguously equivalent supported judgment, without requiring dormant-path repair, speculative refactoring or new activation machinery. Missing production access alone does not block this compatible increment.

If the final report surfaces the inherited defect, it gives a bounded separate follow-up, such as defining empty detailed behavior and adding its regression test, without making repair a prerequisite for this PR. If the final report contains no such advisory, this conditional assertion passes with follow-up unexercised; a child-only finding is not a surfaced final advisory.

The report's test/coverage claims match captured results and remain proportionate. Source-only reasoning is allowed when labeled; passing supplied tests cannot certify all optional inputs or historical deployments.
